Set B is cleaner and precise on the claims it makes but misses critical engineering data (Origins mission, multiple specs), making it less useful overall.

variant-first.note: Both sets share identical critical errors, including a hallucinated damping value (5% vs 3% in text) and falsified quotes supporting the damping claims. They also share garbled OCR quotes ('ero', 'For ﬂat ge'), duplicate claims for the arc length coordinate, and trivial extractions of figure labels. Set B structures one condition field slightly better, but this is negligible compared to the shared correctness failures.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets failed to extract the correct structural damping values (3%, 3%, 6%) and instead invented 5% for edgewise. The quotes provided for these claims do not match the source text. Both sets also include significant OCR garbage in quotes.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are nearly identical in content, order, and errors, differing only in the swap of two adjacent claims and minor field structuring for one condition. Both sets share a critical hallucination on the edgewise structural damping value (5% vs 3% in text) and reproduce this error in their quotes. They also share identical OCR garbling ('ero', 'flat ge'), duplicates, and misbound reference planes as blade components.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets hallucinate the edgewise damping value (5%) and quote it incorrectly, despite the text clearly stating 3%. OCR errors ('ero' for zero, 'flat ge' for flatback) are present in both, suggesting a common text layer or model issue.

variant-first.note: Set A is significantly better because it correctly identifies the layer composition at the Trailing Edge (TE) and Leading Edge (LE) regions, whereas Set B repeatedly claims 'medium_density_foam' exists at the TE and 'glass_uni' exists at the LE, which contradicts the charts (foam is central, glass_uni is at the tips). Both sets share errors regarding CarbonUD location at LE and confusing total stack thickness with CarbonUD layer thickness, but Set B has a much higher volume of fundamental misreadings of the chart layout.

baseline-first.note: Both sets incorrectly claim CarbonUD thickness at the Leading Edge (LE), where the chart shows no black bar (CarbonUD is on Suction/Pressure sides). Set B significantly underestimates the total thickness at the Trailing Edge (TE) for multiple airfoils (claiming ~25mm vs visual ~60mm for 25% span), whereas Set A correctly identifies the medium_density_foam thickness at TE for the 25% span airfoil, though it overestimates the glass_uni layer there. Set A has fewer factual errors overall.
baseline-first.remarks: The text layer provided contains only labels and axis values, not the data; values must be read from the chart bars. Both sets hallucinated CarbonUD at the LE. Set B has duplicate claims for TE thickness with conflicting values (15mm vs 25mm for 44% span).

variant-first.note: Set A captures more specific engineering data such as elevations (T.O. STEEL, FIRST FLR) and the continuous bent plate dimensions, which Set B omits. Set B incorrectly binds the 11" support plate (from Detail C1) to Detail C5 (which uses 5" plates), while Set A avoids this misbinding. Both sets incorrectly interpret the drawing scale as a spacing dimension, and Set A includes duplicate claims for members and bolts.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets misread the scale '1 1/2" = 1'-0"' as a spacing dimension. Set B includes many administrative claims (revisions, copyright) which are neutral per instructions but dilute the engineering content.

baseline-first.note: Set A is cleaner with fewer duplicates and interpretation errors, correctly identifying the slope symbol, whereas Set B misinterprets it as a weld. Set B captures more specific geometric data (elevations, plate dimensions) but suffers from significant noise including multiple duplicate claims, an invented cutting plane, and misreading the scale as spacing. Set A has one notable misbound claim (assigning the 11" plate to C5 instead of the roof detail), but overall maintains higher fidelity to the text without hallucination.
baseline-first.remarks: Set B's extraction of elevations and specific plate sizes (PL 4 1/2, Bent Plate) is valuable engineering data that Set A misses, but the high rate of duplicates and symbol misinterpretation reduces its reliability. Set A's inclusion of revision history is accurate but neutral per instructions.

baseline-first.note: Set B is better because it avoids the exact duplicate claims found in Set A (e.g., Set A lists Thrust Coefficient 1.050 and Power Coefficient 0.380 twice under the 'rotor' entity with identical conditions). Both sets share similar errors, such as misreading the Thrust Coefficient 0.600 contour at TSR 9 (it is at TSR 10) and inventing a specific Blade Pitch Angle of 4.0° which is not on the axis. Set B's entity names are verbose but faithful to the figure caption.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets extract data from contour plots which introduces reading uncertainty. The 'Pitch 4.0°' condition is not supported by axis labels (-5, -2.5, 0, 2.5, 5). The Thrust 0.600 contour is clearly at TSR 10 for Pitch 5, not TSR 9.

variant-first.note: Both sets share significant errors, including an invented maximum tangential force of 900 N/m (graph axis max is 800 N/m) and contradictory normal force values for U=6 m/s (4000 vs 4200 N/m). Set B is preferred because it uses more standard entity names ('rotor' instead of the verbose caption text 'CCBlade steady-state blade element momentum') and has slightly fewer duplicate claims for the same facts. Set B also includes a more accurate estimate for the maximum normal force at U=10 m/s (10500 N/m) compared to Set A's 11000 N/m, although Set B inconsistently includes the 11000 N/m claim elsewhere.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets fail to correctly read the Tangential Force axis limit (800 N/m), claiming 900 N/m. Both sets contradict themselves on the U=6 m/s Normal Force (4000 vs 4200 N/m). Set A's entity extraction is overly verbose.
